title: Miliastra business tool call arguments, contractVersion 1
description: The complete set of arguments any Miliastra business tool may accept. This schema IS the forbidden-passthrough boundary: every field that would let the caller select what runs is absent, and additionalProperties is false so it cannot be smuggled in under another name. A request that fails this schema must be refused before the execution layer is touched, with disposition refusal-before-dispatch.
$comment: Names that must never appear as a tool argument, and the reason, live in plugins/miliastra/contracts/contract.json boundary.forbiddenInToolCall. Because additionalProperties is false, every one of them is rejected structurally, not by a blocklist.

operationId.description: Business idempotency key. Accepted input alias: requestId.

targetHandle.description: Opaque token minted by this project's own discovery step. Accepted input alias: levelHandle. May not contain / \ or :, because a handle is never a path.

expectedRevision.description: An opaque revision token this server returned earlier, never a caller-computed digest. The server recomputes its own revision and compares.

objectIds.description: Ids that must already appear in this run's own receipts. maxItems matches MAX_CLEANUP_IDS 64, MAX_IDS_PER_CALL 64 and the adapter's OWNED_DELETE_TOO_MANY_IDS.

createdByOperationIds.description: On-disk name: createdByRequestIds. Ownership proof leg A.

items.description: Finite. JSON has no NaN or Infinity literal, and the ledger fingerprint is computed with allow_nan=False, so a non-finite value cannot survive either layer.

allOf.$comment: create and save are mutations and therefore require an operationId; the read-only capabilities do not.
